3.evidence_source: Two studies used event-related potentials (ERPs) to examine whether and how divergent thinking and creative achievement are linked to attentional flexibility and cognitive control as indexed by response times and by the amplitude of the anterior N2 ERP component. Both experiments used an oddball paradigm in which participants viewed hierarchical letter stimuli and identified target letters in frequent and rare target trials.
3._section_summary: This abstract describes two studies that utilized event-related potentials (ERPs) and an oddball paradigm to investigate the relationship between divergent thinking, creative achievement, attentional flexibility, and cognitive control. Both experiments involved participants identifying target letters in hierarchical stimuli. The findings indicated that divergent thinkers exhibited greater attentional flexibility and stronger cognitive control during attentional switches, even when controlling for general intelligence, while creative achievement was not associated with these measures.

4._section_summary: This introduction discusses the complex relationship between creativity and attention, differentiating between divergent thinking and real-life creative accomplishments. It reviews prior work linking divergent thinking to attentional flexibility and real-life creativity to 'leaky' attention. The present study aims to investigate the role of attention and cognitive control in creativity, specifically how divergent thinking and creative achievement relate to attentional flexibility and cognitive control. Experiment 1 was a preliminary study to evaluate feasibility, while Experiment 2 improved upon it with a larger sample and by measuring real-life creative achievement and intelligence scores.

It describes the exclusion of two outliers, normality checks, and a repeated measures ANOVA showing significant differences in reaction times across three trial types (frequent target, rare target, no target). 11.evidence_source: The section describes a single investigation, referring to 'Our primary hypothesis' and 'As predicted', indicating one study.
11._section_summary: This section, describing Study X, outlines the hypothesis that higher divergent thinking scores (measured by ATTA) would correlate with greater attentional flexibility (smaller RT oddball effect) and increased cognitive control (larger N2 oddball effect). The findings supported these predictions, showing significant negative correlations between total divergent thinking and RT oddball effect (r = -.64), and between total divergent thinking and N2 oddball effect (r = -.67). Specific correlations for fluency and originality were also reported, while no significant correlation was found with the P3b oddball effect.
